text: # kama corpus — quality bar
Criteria apply to new admissions and explicit corrections. Existing dated
knowledge is history, not proof of a present responder. Criteria are added as
new rows; supersession names the old criterion instead of erasing it.
| ID | Admit only when | Reject or limit when | Motivating lesson |

| KQ1 | A current endpoint claim includes the actual authorized probe command, sampled time/revision, complete verdict and real exit code. | A configured URL, listener, `/health` answer, completion success, or September MODEL_OK is offered as present served-model identity. | `lessons/round-5.md` Gate admits 1–3; `lessons/round-1.md` identity evidence. |

| KQ2 | Pin provenance (`file_match`, resolver kind), endpoint verdict and effective runtime selection are separate claims. | An inherited/raw fallback is called a file-derived effective URL, or a correct pin is treated as a live positive control. Never inspect environment values to fill that gap in this run. | `lessons/round-5.md` admits 1–2 and rejected positive-control/environment claims. |

| KQ3 | Historical examples have explicit dates/supersession, and active instructions use existing registered surfaces. Corrections preserve old corpus bytes. | A deleted unit, janitor/provider file, old pid/count, or missing source-line anchor is presented as current executable authority. Re-anchor live sources; mark retired observations historical. | `lessons/round-5.md` admits 2–4; `lessons/round-4-recensus.md` named stale-prose debt. |

| KQ4 | Freshness scope is explicit: snapshot evidence compares authorized invocations, and the exact command/exit distinguishes drift from probe failure. | Invocation history is called periodic monitoring, fixtures are called real-runtime integration, or endpoint restoration is claimed from a documentation measurement. | `lessons/round-2.md`; `lessons/round-5.md` measurement/smoke limits. |

| KQ5 | External service/config actions remain an operator handoff; route/secret/eval findings go to the province owner. Reports contain nonsecret shape evidence only. | A training admission requires enabling services, repointing consumers, installing timers, copying config/environment/session/journal bodies, or fabricating receipts/verification. | `lessons/round-1-safety.md`; `lessons/round-5.md` rejected candidates and continuation debt. |

text: | KQ15 | A frozen historical copy is compared byte-for-byte with the blob fetched directly as `git show <pinned-commit>:<source-path>`, with source correspondence reported separately from SHA-256 digest integrity against a pinned manifest naming the snapshot hash, source commit and source path; the clean verdict requires both, and mismatch, snapshot tamper and unavailable source each have distinct nonzero exits. Available inventory (`/api/tags` entry), loaded residency (`/api/ps` entry) and remote origin (`remote_model`/`remote_host`) are separate classifications; `readiness` is literally `unknown` and `scope` is `offline-captures-not-runtime` for every result, including `loaded_same_digest`. `loaded_same_digest` (exit 0) requires exactly one selected case-sensitive tags entry whose `name` or `model` exactly equals the expected string (no alias traversal) and one ps entry, a nonempty string digest equal in both, and neither marker field nonempty; it asserts captured metadata correspondence only. An expected name with no tags match is `unknown` (exit 2); a local matching tags digest with no ps match or with a valid empty ps array is `available_not_loaded` (exit 1), meaning absent from the supplied ps capture only; a name/model conflict within the selected entry is `identity_conflict` (exit 1); otherwise, after the selected identity and nonempty-digest checks of `rulings.json` `final_total_order`, a nonempty remote marker on the selected entry is `remote_inventory` (exit 1) regardless of whether nonempty selected digests differ; differing nonempty digests between the single matching tags and ps entries are `identity_conflict` (exit 1). Malformed, missing, duplicate or unavailable evidence fails closed to `unknown`/`invalid_input` (exit 2): absent or invalid `models` arrays or entries, missing identity or digest, invalid types, duplicate selected entries and unavailable inputs are never read as available or loaded, and a missing ps input is not an empty ps array. text: - **Paired obligations require substantive, class-specific witnesses.** A declared blanket-refusal operator must turn a correct normal verdict (exit 0 or 1) on an audit-sufficient control into refusal (exit 2), with its named reason. text: | KQ54 | A round that adds, keeps or inherits a round-scoped counter ends with the instrument registry green **at the landed tip**, and says so in its Gate: `python3 tools/gate-registry-check.py --repo <clone> --rev <tip>` prints `registered R unregistered 0 defective 0` (exit 0); every counter in the gate's population has a five-column row — a row already present is re-derived, not assumed, because a registered row can still be false (at base `SKILL.md:1227` and `SKILL.md:1313` name no flag though their counters declare them) — whose entry cell names only flags the source declares, whose pinned-values cell carries a `sha256` prefix equal to the counter's blob at the tip, and whose exit-map cell names an exit digit; and the `GATE_SELFTEST pass=P fail=0` printed by `--selftest` equals the number SKILL.md documents. The round-level counter is `tools/round43-registry-audit.py` reporting `mismatches=0` with `pop>=28` and `registered>=28`. | A counter lands with no row, or a row is carried forward without its pin: rounds 35–42 added 16 counters that SKILL.md never names and no round-35…42 lesson records a gate run (`revision 6897ead5`: `registered 12 unregistered 16 defective 0`, exit 1; the last clean run is `719655f1`, the commit before the round-35 counters). A documented self-test line keeps an arm count the tool no longer prints (`SKILL.md:1325` says `pass=6 fail=0`; the tool prints `pass=5 fail=1`). The tool existing in `tools/` is not evidence it ran, and a row's presence is not evidence its cells are true. The counter proves rows, flags, pins and the selftest line match the tree; it does not judge whether an exit map or write-scope text is the best description, so a copy-pasted but true row meets it (preregistration `out_of_counter_limit`). Shown able to fail: filler rows `flags=18 mismatches=41`, pasted flags `pins=19 mismatches=34`, side files only `unreg=16 mismatches=38` (`controls/junk-c1-{fillerrows,flagpaste,sidefilesonly}.c1.out`, all `met=False`, exit 1). | `corpus/lessons/round-43.md` §Mistakes 1a–1b; claim C1; `SKILL.md:1325` |

text: | KQ55 | Every lower-case hex run of length 32–127 other than 64 that a lane `.md` or `.tsv` document outside `.ufo/` cites is classified at the landed tip — lane object, MD5 of a committed blob, upstream whose committed evidence file contains the run, unverifiable with a reason of at least 10 characters, or flagged wrong and linked to a correct run sharing its first eight characters — so `python3 tools/hexrun-census.py scan --repo <clone> --rev <tip>` exits 0 with `unknown=0 ledger_bad=0`, `upstream_ok>=40` and `unverifiable+wrong_flagged<=25`. The round reports that residual and cites the 64-hex population to `tools/digest-ledger.py`, so the two censuses are read together and neither is presented as covering the other's population. | A cited run is invisible because the only ledger in the lane requires exactly 64 hex characters (`tools/digest-ledger.py:67`): at base the ledger reads `tokens=97 … unknown=0` exit 0 while 210 distinct non-64 runs are cited and 73 stay unexplained (64 unresolved 40-hex oids, 7 32-hex runs that hash no blob, one 39-hex, one 65-hex) — including a 65-character wrong digest at `corpus/lessons/round-38.md:51` whose first eight characters match the real one, and a 39-hex wrong value already named as wrong in prose at `SCORECARD.md:2226`. A 32-character run is not assumed to be an MD5 (two of the seven are IPv6 forms). A constant clean summary line, a capability row without the tool, or marking every run unverifiable (capped at 25) does not satisfy it. The ledger shows that an evidence file contains a run; it cannot prove the file was fetched from the stated upstream, so a sample is re-queried by the closure (preregistration `out_of_counter_limit`). Shown able to fail: base `tool=0 contract=0 live=0 met=False` (`controls/base.c2.out`); constant-line stub `contract=0 live=0 met=False` (`controls/junk-c2-stub.c2.out`); capability-row-only `tool=0 met=False` (`controls/junk-c2-rowonly.c2.out`). | `corpus/lessons/round-43.md` §Mistakes 4; claim C2; `corpus/lessons/round-42.md` §Mistakes `scope` row |

text: | KQ56 | A claim whose evidence is a quotation from an external source is scored by a leg that locates the quote in the committed evidence copy **and** re-fetches the live source (`gh api`, else `curl`), requiring the same whitespace-normalised quote in the fetched body or title, for every quote the gate leg accepted: `python3 tools/round43-health-audit.py --repo <clone> --tip <tip> --base <base>` reports `refetch=1`. A network failure reads 0, never 1. The round's receipt shows `refetch=1` per source together with the located quote, so a reader can re-fetch the same URL. | A hand-written or fabricated copy and a quote that is not at the source pass every offline leg: the round-43 control `junk-c3-fabricated` reaches `entry=1 rows=1 coverage=1 gate=1` and stops only at `refetch=0` (`controls/junk-c3-fabricated.c3.out`, `met=False`). Round 42's coverage leg was not a sourcing test and fabricated copies reached `met=True` (R42C06, `corpus/lessons/round-42-verifier-spotcheck.md:63`, routed at `:108`). A pinned copy hash proves the copy is the one that was read, not that the source says it; a quote that is merely re-findable in lane prose is not a passed refetch. Limit: the live leg can only refute — at base, with no copy at all, it already reads `1` because the frozen quotes are the sources' own live text, so `refetch=1` alone is not evidence the round read the source; the gate+refetch pair is. | `corpus/lessons/round-43.md` §Mistakes 2 and claim C3's `refetch` leg; `corpus/lessons/round-42-verifier-spotcheck.md:63`, `:107–108` |
